formula: Suede blouson + tonal knit polo + cream wide trouser + suede shoe
why: One statement texture (rich tobacco suede) against calm cream trousers reads instantly expensive with zero logos. The cropped jacket over a full trouser is the exact boxy-top / wide-bottom silhouette that makes him look tall and deliberate.
fit_for_him: Hip-length suede blouson (not longer), cream or ecru wide trousers with a slight break; swap the moc for brown suede derbies or his Premiata.

formula: Navy leather blouson + light-blue shirt + brown pleated wide trouser + black shoe
why: Navy leather is the grown-up, less obvious alternative to a black biker; with a light-blue shirt and brown trousers it hits three of his best colours at once. Confident and sharp for a night out without looking like he tried.
fit_for_him: Keep the blouson cropped at the belt and the trousers full with a break; tuck the shirt, leave the gloves and bag out for Braga.

pieces: khaki layer over a light blue shirt
formula: Soft-colour shearling jacket + light-blue shirt + pale wide denim + black loafer
why: Sage with light blue is an unexpected, soft pairing that looks young and fresh, while the shearling keeps it luxurious. The black loafer stops the denim from feeling too casual.
fit_for_him: Boxy sage or ecru shearling/fleece jacket over a tucked light-blue shirt, relaxed pale jeans that stack on the shoe; a refined loafer, not a sneaker.

formula: Leather jacket + rust knit + check shirt peeking + brown wide trouser + derby
why: Three textures (leather, knit, woven check) in one warm colour family: depth without noise. The check only shows at the hem, so it stays refined rather than lumberjack.
fit_for_him: Shirt tucked so only the collar and hem show; jacket ends at the hip; brown derbies instead of runners.

formula: Olive raglan coat + light-blue shirt + dark brown wide trouser + brown shoe
why: A long olive coat is the easiest way to look quietly expensive in transitional weather, and the light-blue shirt brightens it near the face. Clean enough for meetings, relaxed enough for a weekend away.
fit_for_him: Coat to mid-calf with roomy raglan shoulders; shirt tucked into high-ish wide trousers; brown suede or leather derby.

pieces: navy unstructured wool suit (relaxed jacket + wide trousers)
chambray shirt worn open over a white tee
formula: Soft navy suit + chambray shirt + white tee + black loafer
why: A suit worn like casual clothes: chambray instead of poplin and no tie makes it young and relaxed while still the best-dressed in the room. Navy + light blue is his safest power combo.
fit_for_him: Unstructured, slightly boxy jacket and wide single-pleat trousers; shirt open two buttons with a tank or tee under; black or dark brown loafer.

pieces: oatmeal knit scarf draped over one shoulder
formula: Brown overcoat + draped knit scarf + chocolate knit + charcoal wide trouser + black boot
why: The scarf thrown over the shoulder (not wrapped) is a tiny styling move that makes a standard coat look editorial. Brown on charcoal is richer and warmer than the usual navy-on-black.
fit_for_him: Long, roomy brown coat; chunky scarf draped loose; wide charcoal wool trousers; sleek black boot or derby.

source: MHL. by Margaret Howell – AW26 lookbook
formula: Navy roll-neck + brown wide cord + black derby
why: The simplest look on the board: just two great textures (thick knit, wide-wale cord) in navy and brown. Proof that fabric and fit, not more pieces, are what make an outfit look expensive.
fit_for_him: Roll-neck slightly boxy, sleeves pushed up; cords high-waisted and wide; add a suede overshirt or coat when outside.

pieces: grey knit with shirt collar underneath
formula: Brown overcoat + grey knit over collar + charcoal pleat + black shoe
why: Brown coat over grey tailoring is the quiet-luxury winter uniform: smart enough for a family lunch, relaxed enough for a weekday. The collar peeking above the knit adds polish.
fit_for_him: Single-breasted coat below the knee, crew or V knit over a light-blue or white shirt, pleated charcoal trousers; COS/Arket have all of it.

pieces: matching dark brown wide trousers (soft suit)
formula: Soft brown suit + burgundy roll-neck + black shoe
why: A roll-neck instead of shirt-and-tie turns a suit into something modern and a little moody; burgundy against brown is rich and warm on his skin tone. Perfect when he wants to be the best-dressed at a family event without looking formal.
fit_for_him: Unstructured, slightly boxy jacket and wide trousers in the same brown; fine merino or cashmere roll-neck in burgundy; black or dark brown loafer.

pieces: tan leather jacket with shearling collar
formula: Tan leather jacket + mustard roll-neck + tan wide trouser (tonal camel)
why: Head-to-toe tonal camel looks rich and intentional; the leather and shearling collar add texture so it never looks flat. A real step up from mixing random neutrals.
fit_for_him: Keep everything within one sand-to-camel family; boxy hip-length leather or suede jacket, roll-neck in a slightly darker shade, wide trousers, brown boots.

colours: grey tweed, bottle green, brown, black
formula: Tweed coat + green knit polo + brown layer + dark wide trouser
why: A textured tweed coat is the statement, and the green knit polo at the collar adds a single, considered colour pop. Feels Copenhagen, not countryside.
fit_for_him: Long, relaxed tweed coat; knit polo buttoned up; dark wide wool trousers; sleek black or brown derby.

formula: Ecru boxy jacket + light shirt + dark wide denim + black loafer
why: Ecru on dark indigo is crisp, clean contrast that looks expensive in spring light. The loafer makes jeans office-appropriate.
fit_for_him: Choose a clean, refined cotton or linen jacket (not a rugged workwear chore); dark rigid wide jeans; black loafer or derby.

pieces: check shirt peeking at the hem
formula: Cropped dark blouson + white wide trouser + suede shoe
why: High contrast (dark top, white bottom) with a very short jacket and very wide trousers is the strongest silhouette trick for him. Feels young and Copenhagen-street without a single logo.
fit_for_him: Jacket must hit the waist; white or ecru wide trousers; tan suede derby or Premiata instead of white sneakers.

formula: Leather blouson + muted shirt + burgundy pleated trouser + black loafer
why: Burgundy trousers are the elevating idea: a rich colour in the least expected place, grounded by brown leather and a muted shirt. Very confident, still quiet.
fit_for_him: Wool or fluid twill burgundy pleated trousers (wide, high-ish rise); muted sage or grey shirt buttoned to the top; leather or suede blouson; black loafer.

formula: Sand blouson + white tank + pale pleated denim + black derby
why: All-light palette with one dark anchor (shoes) looks fresh and Mediterranean. Pleated denim is a smart in-between of jeans and trousers.
fit_for_him: Matches his tank-under-a-top rule; skip the wallet chain; pale wide jeans or pleated denim, black derby instead of sneakers.

formula: Sage harrington + grey knit polo + ecru wide trouser + brown suede shoe
why: Sage and ecru are two of his best colours, and the knit polo under a harrington is an easy, grown-up swap for a hoodie. Easy weekend look that still reads considered.
fit_for_him: Harrington at the waist, knit polo zipped halfway, ecru wide trousers; brown suede derby or Gazelle in brown suede.

source: Les Deux – Autumn Winter 2026 studio lookbook
formula: Stone mac + patterned knit + taupe pleated trouser + brown suede shoe
why: The long stone mac makes any outfit look finished, and the patterned knit gives it personality and a young edge. Great for airports and city breaks.
fit_for_him: Knee-length mac open; one interesting knit (pattern or texture) in brown tones; taupe pleated trousers; brown suede shoe, not a chunky runner.

formula: Soft navy jacket + white band-collar shirt + cream pleated trouser + sandal
why: Navy over cream is the classic summer-evening pairing, and the band collar plus sandals make it modern rather than yacht-club. Elegant without effort.
fit_for_him: Unlined, slightly boxy jacket; collarless or camp shirt; fluid cream pleated trousers that pool a little; leather sandal or suede loafer.

formula: Suede blouson + striped tee + matching shorts + black loafer
why: A tonal top-and-shorts set in sand makes shorts look as considered as trousers, and suede in summer is a quiet flex. Loafers keep it grown-up.
fit_for_him: Boxy cropped suede or linen blouson, shorts just above the knee in the same tone, Breton tee, loafers with no-show socks.

formula: Relaxed tonal linen suit + matching shirt + minimal sandal
why: A soft, oversized linen suit in one pale colour is the most elegant summer look there is, and the tonal shirt makes it modern rather than wedding-hire. Instantly 'quietly expensive'.
fit_for_him: Unstructured linen or linen-silk suit in stone/ecru, wide trousers; matching or white camp shirt; suede loafers instead of sandals for a family event.

pieces: slate-blue shirt open at the collar
formula: Olive linen blazer + slate-blue shirt + taupe wide trouser + sandal
why: Three muted colours that don't 'match' but sit perfectly together; a linen blazer over an open shirt is relaxed holiday tailoring. Looks like he knows exactly what he's doing.
fit_for_him: Oversized linen blazer, shirt tucked with top buttons open (tank underneath), taupe or stone wide trousers; sandals or suede loafers.

pieces: printed blue/white collar shirt peeking out
formula: Knit polo + printed collar peeking + indigo wide trouser + leather sandal
why: A knit polo looks far more expensive than a tee, and the printed collar peeking out is a small, playful detail. Brown and indigo are a rich summer pairing.
fit_for_him: Boxy short-sleeve knit polo in brown or navy, wide indigo trousers, leather sandals or suede loafers; the printed collar is optional.
